Here’s a quick rundown of the Canadian federal holidays that give you a “long weekend” (i.e., a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, or an observed holiday that lets you stretch the weekend) in 2023.  (Dates are in 2023 unless noted otherwise.)

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | How it creates a long weekend |
|---------|--------------|--------------------------------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Jan 1 (Sunday) – observed Jan 2 (Monday) | Dec 30‑31 (Sat‑Sun) + Jan 1 (Sun) + Jan 2 (Mon) → 5‑day break |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 (Friday) | Apr 7‑9 (Fri‑Sun) |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 (Monday) | May 20‑22 (Sat‑Mon) |
| **Canada Day** | Jul 1 (Saturday) – observed Jul 3 (Monday) | Jul 1‑3 (Sat‑Mon) |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 (Monday) | Sep 2‑4 (Sat‑Mon) |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 (Monday) | Oct 7‑9 (Sat‑Mon) |
| **Remembrance Day** | Nov 11 (Thursday) – observed Nov 10 (Wednesday) | Nov 11‑13 (Thu‑Sun) |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 (Monday) | Dec 23‑25 (Sat‑Mon) |
| **Boxing Day** | Dec 26 (Tuesday) – observed Dec 27 (Wednesday) | Dec 26‑28 (Tue‑Wed‑Sun) |

> **Quick note:** Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., Family Day in Ontario on Feb 20, St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario on Mar 17, etc.).  Those don’t usually create a long weekend unless they’re observed on a weekday adjacent to a weekend.

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app!
